title: Why remote agent loading became an install-time concern
author: Kody Wildfeuer (@kody-w)
summary: A historical architecture decision moved agent acquisition away from runtime hot loading and toward reviewable local files with explicit installation boundaries.
audience: Agent authors and runtime contributors deciding where package acquisition, review, dependency resolution, and execution should occur.
prerequisites: A local Brainstem install plus a basic understanding of Python imports, file review, and serverless execution boundaries.
applicability: Applies to contributors deciding whether an agent should be acquired during installation or dynamically at runtime.
support_boundary: This is an architectural rationale, not a commitment to add remote-agent loading or a support promise for external package ecosystems.
limitations: This is a local-first runtime decision, not a universal package-management rule. Signed package ecosystems or managed deployment pipelines can make different trade-offs.
status_note: Status as of 2026-08-15: no remote-agent return is scheduled or committed. Treat this as a historical design note; consult current release notes and source before planning work.
